title: The network add-on and the core networking it supersedes
description: How the network add-on started in zap-extensions in November 2021 and how core zaproxy commits from 2022 and 2023 deprecate proxy, connection, client certificate, and HttpSender code in its favour.

chapters.title: A bare add-on on 2021-11-15
chapters.text: The first commit touching addOns/network is "Add bare Network add-on" (2021-11-15), whose body reads "Add basic structure for the network add-on." Within two weeks, commits such as "network: add API to manage root CA certificate" (2021-11-24) follow.

chapters.title: First releases: certificates, then local servers
chapters.text: The CHANGELOG lists 0.0.1 (2021-12-03) with "API endpoints to generate, import (Issue 2280), and obtain the root CA certificate" and server certificate management. 0.1.0 (2022-02-01) adds "Provide HTTP servers/proxies to other add-ons." 0.2.0 (2022-04-06) adds "Management of local servers/proxies, supersedes core functionality;", configuration of aliases and pass-through connections.

chapters.title: Core proxy, connection, and certificate code is deprecated
chapters.text: In zaproxy, "Deprecate and disable proxy related code" is dated 2022-02-09 and its body begins "No longer manage the main nor additional proxies." "Use Network add-on to manage connection options" (2022-05-20) says "Deprecate `ConnectionParam` and remove its usage where possible, the network add-on will manage the connection options." "Use Network add-on to manage client certificates" (2022-05-29) says "Deprecate `OptionsParamCertificate` and remove its usage, the network add-on will manage the client certificates." On 2023-04-28 "Deprecate `Proxy`/`ProxyServer` related methods" says those classes "were superseded by the Network add-on."

chapters.title: The announcement, February 2022
chapters.text: The day after core's "Deprecate and disable proxy related code", the post "New ZAP Networking Layer" (2022-02-10) tells users that the Weekly and Live releases use "a completely different networking stack". It describes the old one as Paros Proxy code on an old and out of date Apache Commons HttpClient, and the new one as living in the network add-on: "All client-side comms (e.g. browser to ZAP) use the Netty library while server-side comms still use HttpClient." The options screens move (Options / Local Proxies becomes Options / Network / Local Servers/Proxies) and a Pass-through tab lists addresses that should not be decrypted. The reasons it gives are support for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, Host header manipulation, lower resource use, and updating the networking code without waiting for a full release. It adds "There is currently no ETA for these changes but they are a priority for us."

chapters.title: A HttpSender implementation based on Apache HttpComponents
chapters.text: The core commit "Deprecate HttpSender implementation classes" (2022-06-07) says those classes "will be superseded by the Network add-on." Three days later, in zap-extensions, "network: provide HttpSender implementation" (2022-06-10) has the body "Add a `HttpSender` implementation based on Apache HttpComponents and set it to core, on newer versions." The CHANGELOG for 0.3.0 (2022-10-27) lists "A newer HTTP client implementation", client certificate management, connection options, and "Promoted to Beta status."

chapters.title: Rate limiting and a later HTTP client update
chapters.text: Release 0.10.0 (2023-07-11) lists "HTTP/HTTPS rate limiting capability." The commit "network: update HTTP client" (2026-09-25) has the body "Update to latest version." The CHANGELOG for 0.30.0 is dated 2026-10-08, and later entries refer to a "HTTP client update in version 0.30.0": 0.32.0 (2026-10-26) lists "Restore unbounded HTTP/1 response header size/count, regressed since the HTTP client update in version 0.30.0 (Issue 9509)." and 0.31.0 (2026-10-16) lists "Reinstate NTLM authentication (Issue 9498)."
